subject.title: feat: Add Anthropic server-side compaction API support

question: Should OpenClaw expose Anthropic server-side compaction as a first-class provider-owned opt-in, and what is its explicit precedence relationship with local compaction and broader Anthropic context-management passthrough?
rationale: The choice defines a durable public configuration and session-continuity contract; source evidence establishes the missing capability but cannot choose the permanent product surface safely.

options.title: Approve focused provider opt-in
options.body: Add a narrowly scoped Anthropic server-side compaction contract, with local compaction remaining the default and explicit tests for request construction and continuation history.

options.title: Fold into broader context management
options.body: Treat this tracker as a requirement of the broader Anthropic context-management design so compaction, editing, and beta handling share one approved provider contract.

options.title: Defer native support
options.body: Keep local compaction as the only supported mechanism until maintainers want to own the provider-specific configuration and transcript semantics.

recommendation.title: Approve focused provider opt-in
recommendation.body: Add a narrowly scoped Anthropic server-side compaction contract, with local compaction remaining the default and explicit tests for request construction and continuation history.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent ownership signals span the compaction configuration, Anthropic transport, wrappers, and the earlier review of this exact decision boundary.
